parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment contains multiple suggestions, each of which is an explicit action. For example, "explain separating set for non-experts" directly tells the authors to add an explanation, and "could cite some more related work, what about SAT solver approaches to causal discovery [2]?" explicitly suggests citing a specific line of work with a reference pointer. These are direct instructions. Moreover, the comment provides concrete details on how to implement these actions. It gives exact quoted phrase replacements ("uncover spurious conditional independences" --> "uncover false negatives"; "sampling noise" --> finite sample sizes), specifies the topic and audience of the requested explanation (separating set, for non-experts), and for the citation specifies exactly what to cite (SAT solver approaches to causal discovery) and points to a specific reference ([2]). The authors thus know exactly what to do and how to do it: replace the identified phrases, add an explanation of the separating set aimed at non-experts, and add the indicated citation. The comment pairs explicit actions with concrete implementation details, matching the rubric level for explicit, fully actionable suggestions.
